# filmopen_forms

*Generated by `scripts/package_digest.py`; regenerate, never edit.*

One form per type in two modes — *Edit* on the viewer's own writable version, *View*, the same boxes locked, on any other (`entity_form.dart`, the type→form door `entity_data_spec.dart`, the per-type tabs — the project's (its subtitle font and size among its general fields, each through one logged setter for a person and an agent, a token pull-down's choice going through a field's own setter where it has one; its treatment's prompt a card of its own, not folded), a character's and a location's (each *General* first and the media card below it, each prompt's card above the place it renders — the Reference prompt above *Reference images*, the Sheet prompt above the sheets, a character's Voice prompt above *Voice samples* (`compareOnly` sections, handed to the card by kind; a comparison pairs their rows instead) —, and *Creator notes*; a scene's open block always shows its First frames and Last frames places, each under its First-frame or Last-frame Prompt card, whatever the media, *Add a place…* offering the other four, a Clip place, where shown, under the block's clip prompt card (its writer handed the block alone and no tokens), their boxes writing the block through `withBlockPrompt`; a box of a prompt's words takes away its `plugin`; each prompt is a `promptSection`, a `FormSectionSpec` whose `body` draws `filmopen_prompt_ui`'s `PromptCard` in place of the section's card, its boxes `promptFields`), an outfit's (`outfit_edit_tab.dart`: General with the name, the description and the condition's chips, then the media card with its Reference prompt and Sheet prompt cards, Garments as rows, Accessories and palette, Creator notes), a prop's (`prop_edit_tab.dart`: General with the kind's chips and *Hero prop*'s switch, then the media card with its Reference prompt and Sheet prompt cards, Handling and sound, Creator notes) and a folder's (`folder_edit_tab.dart`: Name, Kind as chips, Synopsis, Notes; what the folder holds is the pages' card, handed in through `EntityForm.leading`) and a scene's (`scene_edit_tab.dart`: Name, Synopsis, one Location and one Epoch as pull-downs, Characters as rows with *Add character*, its menu naming each character by its picture, and, where the project declares several epochs, an epoch of the character's own, and an outfit where the character has two or more at the entry's epoch, Notes; then the *Dialog and actions* card, `sceneBlocksSections`: on the page the scene's script written there — `ScriptEditor` (`script_editor.dart`) on the form's own draft, a card per block condensed to its line until it is opened and open until the focus goes to another node or a press lands elsewhere — a parked focus, the window's lost or a box letting go, keeps it —, the block open published as the state's script focus and the block the timeline asks for opened while it is in charge, the speaker's pull-down, each character by its picture, the dialogue, direction, action and duration, the block's beats under its duration — position, description, duration, their seconds' total and two warnings that refuse nothing, reordered by menu or drag, `script.beat.*` and `script.beats.*` logs —, its subtitles under them laid out the same, the text plain, `script.subtitle.*` and `script.subtitles.*` logs with the values entered, add, insert, delete, move up and down and a drag, and *Move to scene…* (`script_move.dart`: the target written first under its own next number, a fork where it is not the viewer's, the block then removed and the draft settled before *Moved*); in a comparison a row per block, labelled by its place, its line ending with its beats' and its subtitles' count and seconds) — the epochs editor) — the autosave (`draft_saver.dart`), the JSON editor, the file menu, the write actions (fork, official, pick, label) and `GuardLine`, the red line of development mode. The plug-ins' side of a page too: a card per enabled plug-in on a character's, a location's, a folder's, a scene's and the project's form (`plugin_sections.dart`, fields under `plugins.<tag>.<key>` through the one type door, autosaved and paired in Compare like their neighbours), the plug-in field widgets a card and a plug-in's own page both draw with (`plugin_field_widgets.dart`: a switch, a pull-down, a box, and what an agent's typing parses to), and *Plugins…* on the file menu with its dialog (`plugin_hook_dialog.dart`: a plug-in's rewrite, its progress and *Stop*, the version it wrote opened), all through `filmopen_state`'s seam, of which this package holds two roles: `PluginCatalogueView` for what is installed and `PluginInvocation` for the rewrite it runs.

**Flutter.** 40 files, 17,647 lines under `lib/`; 537 tests in 48 files. Barrel: `lib/filmopen_forms.dart`.

  - `final String stem` — The scene's stem, which the places' identifiers name.
  - `final Map<String, dynamic> draft` — The scene's draft, read again at every build.
  - `final bool enabled` — Whether the block may be written: the form's `FormScope.enabled`.
  - `final ScriptChange onChange` — Every change, through the scene's draft.
  - `final Future<void> Function(String reference)? onDeleteTake` — The page's door once a media entry is flagged deleted; none where null.
  - `final Entity? entity` — The scene's file, which the frame prompts are written in; null draws no prompt.
  - `final DraftSaver? binding` — The page's draft, which a prompt's Generate settles and writes through; null where read-only.
  - `final MentionCandidates? candidates` — The project-backed mention source the prompts' tokens read.
  - `final int candidatesRevision` — Changes exactly when [candidates]' or a [promptCandidates]' list changes.
  - `final PromptMentionCandidates Function(String kind)? promptCandidates` — The form's `@` source of a frame's or a clip's prompt, by the writers' kind (§9.8).
  - `final List<String>? groups` — The groups to draw, in the table's order; null for the Script page's policy.
  - `final String id` — The block's id, which its places name.
  - `final String projectKey` — The film's key (`projectKeyOf`).
  - `final Object tapGroup` — The block card's tap group, which the frame prompts' `@` lists join.
  - `static const frames` — The places shown whatever they hold, each with the prompt it renders from.
  - `static const headers` — The places whose prompt is their header: the frames', and the clip's where its place is shown (§9.3).

### `lib/src/dormant_field.dart`

- **class `DormantFields`** — Draws the fields under it dormant (§9.3, the chat page): each text box its words alone until it is clicked.
  - `const DormantFields({super.key, required super.child})` — Marks [child]'s fields as dormant.
  - `static bool of(BuildContext context)` — Whether [context] is in dormant fields.
- **typedef** `typedef DormantSite` — Where a dormant field stands, for the log (§9.3): its file, its key and its column, `left` or `right`.
- **function** `DormantSite? dormantRow(DormantSite? site, String part)` — [site]'s row named [part] (a relationship's character, an epoch's year), null where [site] is.
- **typedef** `typedef DormantEditorBuilder` — Draws the live editor on [focusNode], which is null where the field is not dormant: the editor as it has always been.
- **class `DormantField`** — A field drawn as its text in a box that looks like the field, holding no editable field (§9.3): a click, a tap or focus by keyboard turns it into its [editor] in place, the caret where the person clicked; leaving the…
  - `const DormantField({ super.key, required this.site, required this.controller, required this.decoration, required this.editor, this.style, this.minL…` — Wraps [editor] at [site].
  - `final DormantSite? site` — Null where the field is not dormant; else where it stands.
  - `final TextEditingController controller` — The text the box draws and the editor edits.
  - `final InputDecoration decoration` — The field's own decoration, the locked look included.
  - `final DormantEditorBuilder editor` — The live editor.
  - `final TextStyle? style` — The field's text style, as given to its editor.
  - `final int minLines` — The editor's minimum lines.
  - `final int maxLines` — The editor's maximum lines; the box clips beyond them.
  - `final bool tabStop` — Whether Tab reaches the box, as it would the editor: not a locked box the editor never let take the focus.
  - `final Widget? Function(BuildContext context)? suffix` — What the editor adds after the decoration's own suffix (a prose box's microphone), drawn with the box.
  - `final bool arrow` — Whether the field is a combo box: the box wears its arrow, which opens the field.
  - `final String? identifier` — The box's semantics identifier, where the editor supplies its own rather than a wrapper around it.
- **class `DormantText`** — A box's text laid out by the render object the live editor uses, so that it wraps, and places each chip, as the editor does (§9.3): one line at the editor's caret gap, its chips given the field's whole width.
  - `DormantText({ super.key, required this.span, required this.textScaler, required this.minLines, required this.maxLines, required this.strutStyle, })…` — Lays out [span] between [minLines] and [maxLines], with [strutStyle] as the editor's.
  - `final InlineSpan span` — The box's text and chips.
  - `final TextScaler textScaler` — The ambient text scale.
  - `final int minLines` — The editor's minimum lines.
  - `final int maxLines` — The editor's maximum lines, clipped beyond them.
  - `final StrutStyle strutStyle` — The editor's forced strut, so a chip does not stretch its line.

### `lib/src/draft_saver.dart`

- **enum `SaveState`** — Where a form's draft stands with respect to its file.
  - values: `clean`, `dirty`, `saving`, `failed`
- **class `DraftSaver`** — The autosave behind every entity form: a working copy of the file's JSON, written a moment after the last change, flushed when the page is left, re-seeded when the file changes underneath.
  - `DraftSaver({required Entity entity, required this.write, this.projectKey, this.reseed, this.reload, this.delay = const Duration(milliseconds: 700)})`
  - `final Future<void> Function(Entity entity, Map<String, dynamic> json) write` — Writes [json] as the new content of [entity]; throws on failure.
  - `final void Function(Map<String, dynamic> before, Map<String, dynamic> after)? reseed` — Updates only boxes whose seeded values this external change replaces.
  - `final Future<void> Function()? reload` — Re-reads the project, for *Discard and re-read* after a refused write.
  - `final Duration delay`
  - `Entity get entity`
  - `Map<String, dynamic> get draft`
  - `bool get disposed` — Whether the form let this draft go — it moved to another file, or went away: what answers late, as a dialog does, must not change it.
  - `int get revision` — Counts the changes made to [draft].
  - `SaveState get state`
  - `Object? get error`
  - `bool get hasUnsavedWork`
  - `bool get touched` — Whether anything has been written into this draft since it was seeded.
  - `void setString(String key, String text)` — A string field: trimmed, removed when empty.
  - `bool entityChanged(Entity next)` — The form received a new [Entity].
  - `Future<bool> flush({String reason = 'flush'})` — Writes now when there is something to write.
  - `Future<void> discardAndReload()` — Throws the draft away and re-reads the file: the way out of a refused write when the other change should stand.
- **class `SaveStatus`** — A failed write's error, for the top right of a form: a saved, unsaved or saving draft says nothing.
  - `const SaveStatus({super.key, required this.saver, this.idPrefix = ''})`
  - `final DraftSaver saver`
  - `final String idPrefix` — Put before the way out's identifiers, so two writable columns on one page each name their own (`right:`).

  - `void watchMentions()` — Follows another project or viewer without touching the boxes' source; called from `build`.
- **function** `Widget localProseBox({ required ProseController controller, required String identifier, required InputDecoration decoration, required ValueChanged<…` — A prose box of a row or a dialog: [controller] in the prose editor under [identifier], the microphone after it where it can be typed into (§9.6), and its committed source sampled as a form field's is.
- **function** `Widget twoPartRow({ required Widget first, Widget? second, Widget? third, Widget? remove, int firstFlex = 1, int secondFlex = 1, bool singleColumn…` — The layout both editors' rows use: two parts — or three, [third] beside [second] — that share a row while there is room and stack when there is not (§9.1), with [remove] at the end however the parts are laid out.
- **class `RelationshipsEditor`** — The rows of [relationshipsField].
  - `const RelationshipsEditor({ super.key, required this.stem, required this.relationships, required this.enabled, required this.label, required this.e…`
  - `final DormantSite? site` — The field's dormant site, null where its boxes are live (§9.3).
  - `final String stem` — The file's stem, in the identifiers: Compare draws two of these.
  - `final List<Map<String, dynamic>> relationships`
  - `final bool enabled`
  - `final String label`
  - `final String emptyText`
  - `final ValueChanged<List<Map<String, dynamic>>> onChanged` — Every row on screen, empty ones included; the caller drops what holds nothing.
- **class `PickerThumb`** — An entity's picture in a picker's entry (§9.3): a [size] square, decoded at the size it is drawn, the type's icon where there is none or it cannot be drawn.
  - `const PickerThumb(this.location, {super.key, required this.type, this.size = 40})`
  - `static const double itemHeight` — The height of a picker's entry that carries a picture.
  - `final MediaLocation? location`
  - `final EntityType type`
  - `final double size`
- **class `MenuLog`** — A pull-down's menu controller that logs each use of it (the logging rule): `<event>.opened` as the menu opens, then one outcome, with `ms` from the opening.
  - `MenuLog(this.event)`
  - `final String event` — The events' prefix, such as `script.speaker`.
  - `Map<String, Object?> data` — What the opening is logged with; the pull-down sets it as it is built.
  - `void end(String outcome, Map<String, Object?> data)` — The menu's outcome — `chosen`, `unchanged`, `refused` — with [data].
- **typedef** `typedef CastOutfit` — An outfit a cast entry may wear: its short name, its name in use and its picture.
- **class `CastEditor`** — The rows of a scene's **Characters**: one per `cast` entry — the character's name in use and short name, its own epoch where the project declares several, its outfit where it has two or more there, and a remove button.
  - `const CastEditor({ super.key, required this.stem, required this.cast, required this.enabled, required this.singleColumn, required this.epochs, requ…`
  - `final List<CastOutfit> Function(Map<String, dynamic> entry)? outfitsOf` — The outfits an entry may wear: its character's at its epoch, else the scene's.
  - `final MediaLocation? Function(String tag)? pictureOf` — A character's picture in the menu, by its short name; none drawn where null.
  - `final VoidCallback? onCreate` — Makes a character and puts it in the scene; null where the page offers no creation (Compare's columns).
  - `final String stem` — The file's stem, in the identifiers: Compare draws two of these.
  - `final List<Map<String, dynamic>> cast`
  - `final bool enabled`
  - `final bool singleColumn`
  - `final List<String> epochs` — The project's epochs where it declares more than one, else none: a row then has no epoch of its own to choose.
  - `final String Function(String tag) epochName`
  - `final String Function(String tag) nameOf`
  - `final bool Function(String tag) isKnown`
  - `final List<String> toAdd` — The project's characters not in the scene yet.
  - `final bool hasCharacters` — Whether the project has any character at all, for the reason an empty menu gives.
  - `final ValueChanged<List<Map<String, dynamic>>> onChanged`

### `lib/src/scene_edit_tab.dart`

- **variable** `const PathBoxes sceneBoxes` — Every box of the scene's form on a path, and what each holds.
- **function** `Map<String, String> sceneFormSeed(Entity entity)` — The text each box of the scene's form starts with.
- **function** `List<String> sceneLocationChoices(FilmProject project, {required Author? viewer})` — The short names of [project]'s locations, in the tree's order, but those in [viewer]'s recycle bin and those wholly discarded (§7).
- **function** `List<String> sceneCharacterChoices(FilmProject project, {required Author? viewer})` — The short names of [project]'s characters, in the tree's order, but those in [viewer]'s recycle bin and those wholly discarded (§7).
- **function** `MediaLocation? Function(String tag) scenePictureOf(FilmProject project, Map<String, dynamic> draft, Author? viewer)` — A character's picture in a scene's pickers, by its short name: at the scene's epoch, as [viewer] sees it (§9.3).
- **function** `List<FormSectionSpec> sceneFormSections(BuildContext context, FormScope scope, FilmProject project)` — A scene's form (Project Specification §10.2): a scene is a series of events at a time and a place, so it names **one** location and **one** epoch and lists its characters.

### `lib/src/script_editor.dart`

- **typedef** `typedef ScriptChange` — One edit of a scene's blocks, handed to the scene's one draft (Software Specification §9.3).
- **typedef** `typedef SpeakerPicture` — The picture a speaker's mark draws: the character's [stem], the entry's [reference] and where its bytes are.
- **typedef** `typedef SpeakerMark` — What a speaker's mark shows, from one resolution of the speaker: the [name] and the [picture], if any.
- **class `ScriptEditor`** — A scene's blocks, edited where they are: the *Edit* tab's *Dialog and actions* card (Software Specification §9.3).
  - `const ScriptEditor({ super.key, required this.stem, required this.draft, required this.enabled, required this.characters, required this.nameOf, req…` — The editor of [draft]'s blocks.
  - `final MediaLocation? Function(String tag)? pictureOf` — A speaker's picture in the pull-down, by short name; none drawn where null.
  - `final SpeakerMark Function(String tag)? speakerMarkOf` — A speaker's mark beside a condensed dialogue block, by short name, its name and picture resolved once; without it, [nameOf] and the character's icon.
  - `final String stem` — The file's stem: the identifiers' and the registry's (§7.1).
  - `final Map<String, dynamic> draft` — The draft whose `blocks` this edits: the form's own working copy, read again at every build.
  - `final bool enabled` — Whether the blocks may be changed: the form's `FormScope.enabled`.
  - `final List<String> characters` — Every character of the project, by short name: the speaker pull-down's second group.
  - `final String Function(String tag) nameOf` — The name a speaker is shown by.
  - `final ScriptChange onChange` — Every change, through the scene's draft.
  - `final void Function(int index)? onMove` — Opens *Move to scene…* for the block at a position; null disables the item, saying [moveUnavailable].
  - `final String? moveUnavailable` — Why *Move to scene…* is disabled, where [onMove] is null.
  - `final bool singleColumn` — One field a row: below `Breakpoints.singleColumn` of pane, and in a narrow column.
  - `final MentionCandidates? candidates` — The project-backed mention names and pictures the script's prose fields share, one source updated in place.
  - `final int candidatesRevision` — Changes exactly when [candidates]' list or a [promptCandidates]' changes: every prose box made re-projects then, never on another build.
  - `final PromptMentionCandidates Function(String kind)? promptCandidates` — The form's `@` source of a frame's or a clip's prompt, by the writers' kind (§9.8); without one the prompt's box offers nothing.
  - `final bool projectWritable` — Whether the project may be written at all, which an empty locked card's words follow: a fork where it may.
  - `final String? projectKey` — The film's key (`projectKeyOf`), which a block's media places name their insertions by; null draws none.
  - `final Future<void> Function(String reference)? onDeleteTake` — The page's door once a block's media entry is flagged deleted: it settles the draft, then asks the state.
  - `final Entity? entity` — The scene's file, which a block's frame prompts are written in; null draws no frame prompt.
  - `final DraftSaver? binding` — The page's draft, which a frame prompt's Generate settles and writes through; null where the blocks are read-only.
- **variable** `final scriptEditorCensus` — The script editor's work, counted for the keystroke's census test.

### `lib/src/script_move.dart`

- **function** `Future<void> showMoveBlockDialog(BuildContext context, { required FilmProject project, required Entity scene, required String blockId, required Dra…` — Opens *Move to scene…* for the block [blockId] of [scene], whose draft [saver] holds.
- **class `MoveBlockDialog`** — The dialog of *Move to scene…*: the film's other scenes in script order, and the move.
  - `const MoveBlockDialog({ super.key, required this.project, required this.scene, required this.blockId, required this.saver, required this.remove, })` — The dialog for the block [blockId] of [scene].
  - `final FilmProject project` — The film the block is in, as the page had it when the menu was opened.
  - `final Entity scene` — The scene's version the block is in: the page's.
  - `final String blockId` — The block's id, by which it is read again once every draft is written.
  - `final DraftSaver saver` — The source's draft, whose block moves and which is settled before *Moved*: the page's own, which must still be the draft open on the scene's file when the move writes and when it removes.
  - `final void Function(void Function(Map<String, dynamic> draft) apply) remove` — A structural change of the source's blocks, through its draft.

### `lib/src/write_actions.dart`

- **class `WriteRefusal`** — Why a write was not done, in the user's language, and whether a re-read would let it through.
  - `const WriteRefusal(this.message, {this.stale = false})`
  - `final String message`
  - `final bool stale`
- **typedef** `typedef Asked` — The film a dialog is asked for in, read through the app's container, which outlives the page.
- **class `WriteActions`** — The writes the entity page offers, with their failure messages in one place.
  - `const WriteActions(this.ref, this.project, this.entity, this.viewer)`
  - `final WidgetRef ref`
  - `final FilmProject project`
  - `final Entity entity`
  - `final Author? viewer`
  - `static Asked ask(BuildContext context)` — The film open now, bound before a dialog's opening waits for the drafts (`stillOpen`).
  - `static bool stillOpen(Asked asked)` — Whether the film [asked] names is still the film open (`ProjectController.isCurrent`).
  - `Entity get current` — The entity as the film knows it now, a write of the app's own that landed and is not yet published included.
  - `Future<void> fork(BuildContext context, {Entity? of})` — Forks the page's version — or [of], another version the page shows (Compare's left column) — and opens the fork.
  - `Future<WriteRefusal?> declareEpoch(BuildContext context, String label, {int? year})` — Declares an epoch labelled [label] on the project version the page shows, for the Add epoch dialog (§8.2).
  - `Future<VersionStem?> createAtEpoch(BuildContext context, EntityGroup group, String epoch, { required String sourceEpoch, required Entity source, re…` — Makes the viewer's first version of [group] at the missing [epoch], and says so (§8.2).
  - `Future<WriteRefusal?> createOutfit(BuildContext context, String character, String epoch, String name)` — Makes the viewer's outfit named [name] for [character] at [epoch], for the New outfit dialog.
  - `Future<void> setOfficial(BuildContext context, bool official)` — The star.
  - `Future<void> setPick(BuildContext context)` — Makes this page's version, as the project holds it now, the viewer's pick (§13.4).
  - `Future<void> abandonPickOf(BuildContext context, Entity target)` — The banner's two answers, which name the picked version — not always the one on screen — and each say so only when they wrote something, a refusal being a message of its own.
  - `Future<void> keepPickOf(BuildContext context, Entity target)` — Keeps the viewer's stale pick of [target] in use and re-dates it, which clears its stale warning (§13.2).
  - `Future<void> setLabel(BuildContext context, String? label)` — Writes [label] as the version label of this page's file as the project holds it now, an empty one removing it.
  - `Future<({VersionStem? stem, WriteRefusal? refusal})> tryFork(BuildContext context)` — Forks without navigating, and without turning a refusal into a snackbar.
  - `Future<({VersionStem? stem, WriteRefusal? refusal})> tryForkWith(BuildContext context, Entity source, Map<String, dynamic> json, { required String…` — Forks [source] as the viewer's next version holding [json], written once, in the film [film] and against [source]'s file as it was read (`ProjectController.fork`).
  - `Future<WriteRefusal?> trySaveOver(BuildContext context, Entity source, Map<String, dynamic> json, { required String film, })` — Writes [json] into [source], the viewer's own version, against its file as it was read and in the film [film], never a later read of it: a change made to what [source] held is refused where the file changed since.
  - `Future<WriteRefusal?> trySave(BuildContext context, Entity base, Map<String, dynamic> json)` — Saves [json], a whole document the person built from [base], as the entity's new content, against [base]'s text: a write that landed since — the app's own included — refuses it as stale, never put back (§7.5).
  - `Future<void> visit()` — Records that the viewer has the entity's media on screen (§13.4), through the state's one door; it shows nothing, since a visit is bookkeeping and a refusal is only logged.
  - `Future<void> deleteTake(BuildContext context, String reference)` — Deletes the file of the take [reference] names, once the entry's `deleted` has reached the file (§9.0).
  - `Future<void> reload()` — Re-reads the project (after a refused write, so the next attempt sees the current file).
  - `Future<T?> run<T>(BuildContext context, Future<T> Function() write, {String op = 'run', Map<String, Object?> values = const {}, Stopwatch? watch})` — Runs one write, named [op] in the log with the [values] it works on, and turns its refusals into messages.
